column1: # Customer lines may use the game's tokens: [g:male|female|neutral] and [r:informal|formal].
# Each set of lines has a <set>_count entry: keep it equal to the number of variants below it
# and keep the counts the same in every language file.
# --- Deal panel section and button tooltips

column2: Come Back Tomorrow
Send this customer away and have them return tomorrow.
Ask
Pay
Restock
They come back tomorrow with a new load.
No customer at the counter.
This customer already came back at your request.
They are already coming back tomorrow.
You blackmailed or threatened this customer. They won't do you any favours.
This customer can't be asked to come back.
This person has information that is relevant now.
Tourists are only passing through. They won't be here tomorrow.
This customer came because of what is happening on the station. They can't wait until tomorrow.
This customer keeps their own schedule.
You need {0}.

column1: # --- Word that joins two pieces of bad news in one message

column2: Additionally...
Fine, I'll come back tomorrow.
Tomorrow, then. Don't make me regret it.
All right. Same counter, tomorrow.
I can wait a day. Just be open when I get here.
Sure. It's not like I'm leaving this tin can.
Tomorrow works. Keep the shutter up for me.
If it helps you out, fine. One day.
Okay. One more lap of the ring and I'll see you tomorrow.
Fine. My shift ends the same time tomorrow anyway.
Tomorrow, sure. Down here one day looks like the next.
All right. I'll swing by after the water line.
Okay, okay. Tomorrow. Save me a spot.
Very well. I shall return tomorrow.
I suppose my calendar can bear it. Tomorrow.
If you insist. Do try to be prepared this time.
Tomorrow, then. I shall have my assistant make a note.
Tomorrow. Same place, fewer questions.
Fine. I've got other stops tonight anyway.
All right. But I don't wait twice.
Tomorrow. And you didn't see me today.
No. I'm here now.
I haven't got time to come twice.
Now or never.
I don't stand in line for fun. No.
Tomorrow I've got a shift. It's today or nothing.
I walked half the station to get here. We do this now.
Not happening. Are we doing business or not?
A day is a long time on this station. No.
Tomorrow I'm pulling a double shift. Now.
I climbed six decks of stairs for this. No.
The lifts are dead again. I'm not making this trip twice.
By tomorrow my credits could be gone. Today.
I did not descend all this way to be turned out.
My time is worth rather more than your shop. No.
Out of the question. One does not make this journey twice.
Tomorrow I have engagements. Proper ones.
I don't show up in the same place two days running.
Tomorrow there could be a patrol at your door. No.
People like me don't make appointments.
No. Now, or I find another counter.
For that money? See you tomorrow.
Deal. Tomorrow.
Pleasure doing business. I'll be back.
Credits for walking away? Easiest job I've had all week.
That covers the trip. Tomorrow, then.
You pay, I wait. Simple.
Fine by me. Same time tomorrow.
I'll take it. Just don't expect me early.
That's half a shift's pay for doing nothing. Tomorrow!
You're paying me to go home? Done.
For that I'd come back three times.
That's dinner sorted. See you tomorrow.
Compensation. How very civilised. Tomorrow.
That will cover the inconvenience. Barely.
Acceptable. I shall return tomorrow.
I see you understand how matters are settled. Until tomorrow.
Now you're speaking my language. Tomorrow.
Money first. That I like. See you tomorrow.
For that, I was never here today.
Paid to vanish for a day? Easy.
I'm back, like you asked.
You said today. So here I am.
Here I am again.
Tomorrow came. So did I.
Second visit. Let's make this one count.
I waited a whole day for this. Remember me?
Back again. I hope you're ready this time.
A deal's a deal. I'm here.

column1: # --- Greeting when they return: lower levels

column2: Got off shift early for this. I'm back.
Told you I'd come. Lower decks keep their word.
Same boots, same face. Back like we said.
The lifts worked today. Lucky you.

column1: # --- Greeting when they return: upper levels

column2: I have returned, as arranged.
I had to sleep in a dump down here. I trust it will be worth it.
You asked for today. Here I am, against my better judgement.
A second visit to this deck. Let us not waste it.

column1: # --- Greeting when they return: black market

column2: I'm back. Nobody followed me.
You said today. I'm here.
Same business as yesterday. Let's keep it quick.
Told you I'd show. I keep my word. Mostly.

column1: # --- Second message of a returned seller: same goods as yesterday

column2: Same goods as yesterday. Have a look.
Nothing's changed since yesterday. It's all here.
Everything I showed you is still for sale.
I kept it all for you. Take your pick.

column1: # --- Second message of a returned buyer: still wants the same

column2: I still want the same thing. Show me what you've got.
My credits are still good. What do you have for me?
Nothing's changed. I'm still buying.
Same wishes as yesterday. Let's see your counter.

column1: # --- Second message of a returned customer who sells and buys

column2: Same goods, same shopping list. Let's trade.
I'm still selling and still buying. Your move.
Nothing's changed on my side. Let's do business.

column1: # --- Second message: part of the seller's goods was swapped overnight

column2: I couldn't hold on to everything. Some of it sold overnight, so I brought other things.
Part of yesterday's load is gone. I filled the gaps with something else.
A neighbour needed a few of those more than you did. I got replacements, though.
Someone made me an offer last night. What's missing, I swapped for other stuff.
Not everything survived the night. I brought what I could instead.
A few things went missing from my bunk. Here's what I've got in their place.
I had to trade some of it for a place to sleep. The rest is here, plus a few extras.
You'll notice some changes. A day is a long time to keep goods.
Half my bag got "inspected" at a checkpoint. I topped it up with other things.
I had to pay a debt with some of it. Don't worry, I brought replacements.

column1: # --- Second message: a seller of contraband or stolen goods swapped part of them overnight

column2: I had to dump part of it. Too many scanners. I brought something else instead.
A patrol came through my block last night. Some of it went down the recycler.
I couldn't sit on all of it another night. I moved some and picked up other things.
Part of the load found another buyer. One who didn't make me wait.
I got nervous and flushed a few pieces. Here's what's left, plus some extras.
My contact took some of it back. This is what I got instead.
Things like this don't keep. Some of it is gone, some of it is new.
I had to bribe a guard with part of the goods. I filled the gaps.
Somebody was asking questions. I traded the worst of it away.
Half of it was too risky to carry twice. The rest is here, with replacements.

column1: # --- Second message: the buyer has fewer credits than yesterday

column2: I've got less to spend than yesterday. The night was expensive.
Somebody lifted part of my credits in the corridor. The rest will have to do.
I had to pay for a bunk. My budget is thinner today.
Bad news: half my money went on a debt last night.
I lost a few hands of cards while waiting. Fewer credits today.
A "fee" at the checkpoint ate into my budget.
The lift toll, the bunk, the food... I can't spend what I had yesterday.
I'm not as rich as I was yesterday. Don't ask.
Not all of my credits made it through the night.
Rent came due this morning. There's less left for shopping.

column1: # --- They came back and were sent away without a single trade

column2: You made me come back for nothing?
Two trips, and not one deal. Unbelievable.
I gave up a day for this. People will hear about it.
So yesterday was a joke? Good to know.
I don't understand. You asked me to come back!
I slept on a bench in the transit hall to be here. For this?
Next time, just say no on the first day.
You wasted my day. I won't forget that.
I skipped a shift for you. A whole shift!
What was the point of all this?
I told people this shop was all right. My mistake.
Was it something I said? ... No? Then why am I here?
A patrol stopped me twice on the way. For nothing, as it turns out.
I crossed three decks. Twice.
You have a strange way of doing business.
Don't ask me to come back again. Ever.
I could have gone to another counter yesterday.
Unbelievable. Just unbelievable.
I paid for a bunk on this deck just to be here on time.
Fine. But everyone I know will hear how you treat people.

column1: # --- They came back with contraband or stolen goods and are arrested

column2: You set me up!
You told me to come back just for this?!
This was a trap from the start!
Ask accepted (same goods tomorrow
Tomorrow instead? Fine. But that makes it my day from now on.
All right, I'll move my round. See you tomorrow.
One day later, then. Every week.
My week has room for it. Tomorrow.
Fine. I'll keep the load packed.
Ask refused
I come once a week. Today is the day.
My week is planned. Yes or no.
No. Same day as always.
I've got other stops tomorrow. Today or next week.
I keep to my round. I'm not changing it.
Pay accepted
For that I'll rearrange my week. Tomorrow.
That pays for the detour. See you tomorrow.
Fine. My day just moved.
Credits for a day's delay? My round can bend.
All right. I'll hold the load until tomorrow.
when they return with the same goods
A day late, as asked. Same load as yesterday.
It all stayed packed. Nothing changed.
Here I am. Everything from yesterday is still here.
Same crates, one day older. Have a look.
I held it all back. This is my day now.
always works
A different load? For that money I'll repack tonight.
Fine. I'll take this back and bring something else tomorrow.
Paid in advance for a fresh round? See you tomorrow.
Not to your taste? I'll see what else I can get by tomorrow.
All right. New load tomorrow, no promises what's in it.
Paid up front? Then tomorrow you get a whole new set of crates.
Fine by me. Tonight I'll see what my contacts have left.
Your credits, my legwork. Tomorrow you'll see something different.
I'll put this lot back in storage and bring other crates.
Nothing here you like? I know a couple of warehouses that owe me.

column1: # --- Restock: when they return with new goods

column2: New load, as paid for. Have a look.
Repacked everything last night. This is what I've got now.
Yesterday's goods are gone. These are fresh.
Different crates today. Maybe these suit you better.
You wanted something new. Here it is.
Fresh crates, straight off the cargo lift. Take your pick.
Spent half the night hauling these. Don't tell me you don't like them either.
Like I said yesterday: a different load. See for yourself.
My contacts came through. Let's see if this is more to your taste.
Nothing left from yesterday's crates. All new stock.
Carry this around another day? Not a chance.
With what I've got on me? No. Now, or forget it.
I'm not walking the corridors twice with this.
Every scanner between here and my bunk is a risk. No.
Sleep with this under my bed? No.
That covers the risk. Tomorrow.
Fine. For that I'll hide it one more night.
That pays for my nerves. See you tomorrow.
That buys one more walk past the checkpoints.
Risk has a price. You just paid it.

column1: # --- Seller with stolen goods refuses Ask

column2: These need to be gone today. Not tomorrow.
Someone is already looking for this stuff. No.
I'm not holding on to these another night.
By tomorrow somebody will have noticed it's missing.
Hot goods don't keep. Today.

column1: # --- Seller with stolen goods accepts Pay

column2: For that I'll keep them hidden one more day.
Fine. But if anyone asks, I was never here.
That buys one day. Tomorrow.
I know a locker nobody checks. Tomorrow.
All right. One more night looking over my shoulder.

column1: # --- Seller with contraband AND stolen goods refuses Ask

column2: Stolen and illegal, and I'm supposed to come back? No.
Every hour I carry this is an hour too many.
We both know what this is. Now or never.
If they catch me with this, it's two charges. No.
I want this out of my hands, not back in my bag.

column1: # --- Seller with contraband AND stolen goods accepts Pay

column2: That's a lot of risk in that price. Tomorrow.
One more night with all of this. I'll remember that.
Money talks. I'll be back.
For that price I'll risk both charges. Tomorrow.
Somebody really wants this. Fine.

column1: # --- Options of the mod (gear button in the Mods menu)

column2: Easy Mode - 50% cheaper
Pay and Restock cost half the usual price.
Allow Restock for All
The Restock button is offered for every seller, not only the weekly ones. They come back tomorrow with a new load.
Ask Anyone
WARNING: may break the game! Removes every limit on who can be asked to come back tomorrow: story characters, tourists, event customers, customers who already came back... Use at your own risk.
